 .et_pb_row_inner { width: 100%; }
 .et_pb_column { position: relative; } </style> <style id="sie-custom-header-inline">/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 SIE Custom Header — v1.1.2
 Zero-CLS, no JavaScript layout shifts.
 No panoramic image — lean 64px nav bar only.
 backdrop-filter is intentionally NOT used on .sie-hdr__bar.
 Any element with backdrop-filter becomes a CSS containing block for
 position:fixed descendants, which would trap the user-ui mobile bottom bar
 (position:fixed; bottom:0) inside the header instead of the viewport.
 ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
/* ── Root variables ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
:root {
 --sie-hdr-brand:       #0056b3;        /* SIE brand blue                      */
 --sie-hdr-brand-light: #1a6fc4;
 --sie-hdr-bar-h:       64px;           /* nav bar height — fixed, prevents CLS */
 --sie-hdr-bar-bg:      #0056b3;        /* solid — no backdrop-filter needed   */
 --sie-hdr-bar-border:  rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15);
}
/* ── Wrapper ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr {
 width: 100%;
 display: block;
 min-height: var(--sie-hdr-bar-h);
 /* Own stacking context so dropdowns render above Divi page content */
 position: relative;
 z-index: 1000;
}
/* ── Navigation bar ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__bar {
 height: var(--sie-hdr-bar-h);
 background: var(--sie-hdr-bar-bg);
 /* NO backdrop-filter here — it would trap position:fixed children
 (user-ui mobile bottom bar) inside this element instead of viewport */
 border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sie-hdr-bar-border);
}
.sie-hdr__inner {
 max-width: 1280px;
 height: 100%;
 margin: 0 auto;
 padding: 0 24px;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 32px;
}
/* ── Logo ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__logo {
 flex-shrink: 0;
 text-decoration: none;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
}
.sie-hdr__logo-img {
 height: 54px;
 width: auto;
 display: block;
}
.sie-hdr__logo-text {
 font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
 font-size: 17px;
 font-weight: 700;
 color: #fff;
 letter-spacing: -0.01em;
 white-space: nowrap;
}
/* ── Desktop navigation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__nav {
 flex: 1;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list {
 list-style: none;
 margin: 0;
 padding: 0;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list li {
 position: relative;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list a,
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {
 display: inline-flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
 padding: 8px 14px;
 font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
 font-size: 14px;
 font-weight: 500;
 color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
 text-decoration: none;
 border-radius: 8px;
 transition: background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease;
 white-space: nowrap;
 min-height: 48px; /* WCAG touch target */
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {
 background: none;
 border: none;
 cursor: pointer;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list a:hover,
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle:hover,
.sie-hdr__has-dropdown:hover > .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12);
 color: #fff;
}
/* ── Resources dropdown ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__dropdown {
 display: none;
 position: absolute;
 top: calc(100% + 6px);
 left: 0;
 min-width: 240px;
 background: #fff;
 border-radius: 12px;
 box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18);
 padding: 8px 0;
 list-style: none;
 margin: 0;
 z-index: 9999;
}
/* CSS-only hover on desktop */
@media (hover: hover) {
 .sie-hdr__has-dropdown:hover > .sie-hdr__dropdown,
 .sie-hdr__has-dropdown:focus-within > .sie-hdr__dropdown {
 display: block;
 }
}
/* JS-toggled state (mobile / keyboard) */
.sie-hdr__has-dropdown.is-open > .sie-hdr__dropdown {
 display: block;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown li {
 margin: 0;
 padding: 0;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown a {
 display: block;
 padding: 10px 18px;
 font-size: 13.5px;
 color: #003B73;
 font-weight: 500;
 border-radius: 0;
 min-height: unset;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown a:hover {
 background: #f0f7ff;
 color: #0b5394;
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle svg {
 transition: transform 0.2s ease;
}
.sie-hdr__has-dropdown.is-open .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle svg,
.sie-hdr__has-dropdown:hover .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle svg {
 transform: rotate(180deg);
}
/* ── Mobile hamburger ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__hamburger {
 display: none;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: center;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 5px;
 width: 44px;
 height: 44px;
 background: none;
 border: none;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 0;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 margin-left: auto;
}
.sie-hdr__hamburger span {
 display: block;
 width: 22px;
 height: 2px;
 background: #fff;
 border-radius: 2px;
 transition: transform 0.25s ease, opacity 0.25s ease;
}
/* Animate to ✕ when open */
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(1) {
 transform: translateY(7px) rotate(45deg);
}
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(2) {
 opacity: 0;
}
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(3) {
 transform: translateY(-7px) rotate(-45deg);
}
/* ── User-UI icon bar integration ────────────────────────────────────────────
 user-ui.php's desktop bar uses position:absolute; top:20px; right:30px — that
 was designed for Divi's header context. Inside our flex .sie-hdr__inner we
 need it as a normal flex child instead.
 Fixed-position children (auth drawer, mobile bar, destinations panel) are
 unaffected — position:fixed is always viewport-relative provided no ancestor
 has backdrop-filter, transform, or perspective (we intentionally avoid all
 three on .sie-hdr__bar).
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr .se-user-menu-wrapper {
 position: static !important;
 top: auto !important;
 right: auto !important;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 margin-left: auto;
}
/* Align our mobile breakpoint (860px) with user-ui's desktop/mobile split */
@media (min-width: 861px) {
 .sie-hdr .se-user-menu-wrapper {
 display: flex !important;
 }
}
@media (max-width: 860px) {
 .sie-hdr .se-user-menu-wrapper {
 display: none !important;
 }
}
/* Leonardo icon in the nav bar.
 user-ui's default .se-ai-icon is 86×86 px (fine for the mobile bottom bar),
 but that overflows our 64px-tall nav bar. Override to a crisp 36px square —
 the webp source is already high-res so it stays sharp at 2× on retina. */
.sie-hdr .se-ai-icon {
 width:  36px !important;
 height: 36px !important;
 border-radius: 50%;
 object-fit: cover;
}
/* Icon colours inside the header.
 user-ui defaults: map icon is #2f6fed (dark blue) and heart is #F44336 (red).
 The map icon is nearly invisible on our #0056b3 bar — lift all icons to white.
 The heart keeps its red via the !important below so favourited items still pop. */
.sie-hdr .se-shortlist-link,
.sie-hdr .se-dest-desktop-btn,
.sie-hdr .se-user-icon {
 color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.85) !important;
}
.sie-hdr .se-shortlist-link:hover,
.sie-hdr .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover,
.sie-hdr .se-user-icon:hover {
 color: #fff !important;
}
/* Fav heart — keep the red so it reads as "save" */
.sie-hdr .se-fav-desktop-link {
 color: #ff6b6b !important;   /* slightly lighter red, readable on blue */
}
.sie-hdr .se-fav-desktop-link:hover {
 color: #ff4444 !important;
}
/* ── Responsive ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
@media (max-width: 860px) {
 :root {
 --sie-hdr-bar-h: 56px;
 }
 .sie-hdr {
 min-height: var(--sie-hdr-bar-h);
 }
 .sie-hdr__hamburger {
 display: flex;
 }
 .sie-hdr__nav {
 /* Hidden off-screen when closed — no layout shift */
 position: absolute;
 top: var(--sie-hdr-bar-h);           /* flush below the nav bar */
 left: 0;
 right: 0;
 background: var(--sie-hdr-bar-bg);
 /* NO backdrop-filter — same reason as .sie-hdr__bar */
 padding: 12px 0 20px;
 clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0);       /* collapses upward — no CLS */
 transition: clip-path 0.3s ease;
 z-index: 9998;
 }
 .sie-hdr__nav.is-open {
 clip-path: inset(0);
 }
 .sie-hdr__nav-list {
 flex-direction: column;
 align-items: flex-start;
 gap: 0;
 padding: 0 16px;
 }
 .sie-hdr__nav-list a,
 .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {
 width: 100%;
 font-size: 15px;
 padding: 12px 8px;
 border-radius: 8px;
 }
 .sie-hdr__dropdown {
 position: static;
 box-shadow: none;
 border-radius: 0;
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
 padding: 4px 0 4px 16px;
 margin: 4px 0;
 }
 .sie-hdr__dropdown a {
 color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8);
 font-size: 14px;
 }
 .sie-hdr__dropdown a:hover {
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
 color: #fff;
 }
}
@media (max-width: 480px) {
 .sie-hdr__inner {
 padding: 0 16px;
 gap: 16px;
 }
}
/* Hover-gap fix: invisible bridge spanning the 6px gap between the nav item
 and the dropdown panel, so the cursor never "leaves" while crossing. */
.sie-hdr__dropdown::before {
 content: "";
 position: absolute;
 top: -10px;
 left: 0;
 right: 0;
 height: 10px;
}
/* Anti-FOUC guard for body-rendered overlays: their own CSS arrives 20KB+

 first paint — each component's .open/.is-open rules override these. */
.sie-dest-panel,
#sie-auth-drawer,
#sie-lead-form-drawer,
.sie-finder-overlay {
 position: fixed;
 inset: 0;
 opacity: 0;
 visibility: hidden;

#sie-auth-drawer { position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:2147482000; background:rgba(12,113,195,.42); opacity:0; visibility:hidden; pointer-events:auto; transition:opacity .25s ease; backdrop-filter:saturate(1.05) blur(1px); }
#sie-auth-drawer.open { opacity:1; visibility:visible; }
#sie-auth-drawer .sie-auth-inner { position:absolute; top:0; right:0; height:100%; width:min(560px,100%); background:linear-gradient(180deg,#ffffff 0%,#f7fbff 100%); box-shadow:-12px 0 24px rgba(0,0,0,.16); padding:26px 24px 28px; overflow:auto; will-change:transform,opacity; transform:translateX(28px); opacity:0; transition:transform .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1),opacity .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); z-index:2147482100; }
#sie-auth-drawer.open .sie-auth-inner { transform:translateX(0); opacity:1; }
@media (max-width:768px){
 #sie-auth-drawer .sie-auth-inner { top:auto; bottom:0; right:auto; left:0; width:100%; height:85vh; border-top-left-radius:16px; border-top-right-radius:16px; box-shadow:0 -12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.16); transform:translateY(28px); }
 #sie-auth-drawer.open .sie-auth-inner { transform:translateY(0); }
}
.sie-auth-close { background:transparent; border:0; font-size:30px; line-height:1; cursor:pointer; position:absolute; right:14px; top:10px; color:#0b3770; opacity:.9; }
.sie-auth-close:hover { opacity:1; }
.sie-auth-title { margin:0 0 6px; font-size:1.6rem; font-weight:800; color:#0b3770; }
.sie-auth-intro { margin:0 0 16px; color:#163b6b; font-size:1.02rem; line-height:1.45; }
.sie-hero { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; background:#eef5ff; border:1px solid #dbe8ff; border-radius:14px; padding:10px 12px; margin:10px 0 14px; }
.sie-hero-left { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; }
.sie-hero-avatar { width:44px; height:auto; border-radius:50%; }
.sie-hero-copy { display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; font-size:.92rem; color:#0b3770; }
.sie-hero-line { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; }
.sie-hero-line i { font-size:.95rem; color:#1e66f5; }
.sie-toggle { --pad:4px; position:relative; display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; background:#e9f2ff; border-radius:999px; padding:var(--pad); margin-bottom:12px; width:fit-content; min-width:320px; }
.sie-toggle-btn { position:relative; z-index:1; border:0; background:transparent; padding:10px 18px; border-radius:999px; font-weight:800; color:#0b3770; cursor:pointer; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; line-height:1; }
.sie-toggle-btn.active { color:#fff; }
.sie-toggle-pill { position:absolute; top:var(--pad); left:var(--pad); width:calc(50% - var(--pad)); height:calc(100% - var(--pad)*2); border-radius:999px; background:#1e66f5; box-shadow:0 4px 10px rgba(12,113,195,.28); transition:transform .25s ease; will-change:transform; }
.sie-auth-panel label { font-weight:600; margin-top:12px; display:block; color:#003B73; }
.sie-label-strong { font-weight:800; color:#0f172a; font-size:1.05rem; }
.sie-auth-panel .input { width:100%; padding:12px 14px; border:1px solid #d4dceb; border-radius:12px; background:#fff; transition:box-shadow .15s ease,border-color .15s ease; }
.sie-auth-panel .input:focus { outline:none; border-color:#1e66f5; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(30,102,245,.14); }
.sie-auth-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; border:0; padding:12px 18px; border-radius:999px; cursor:pointer; background:#1e66f5; color:#fff; font-weight:800; box-shadow:0 6px 18px rgba(30,102,245,.18); transition:transform .05s ease,box-shadow .2s ease; }
.sie-auth-btn:hover { box-shadow:0 10px 24px rgba(30,102,245,.22); }
.sie-auth-btn:active { transform:translateY(1px); }
.sie-consent { margin:10px 0 4px; }
.sie-consent-label { font-size:.95rem; color:#0b3770; }
.sie-consent input[type="checkbox"] { margin-right:8px; vertical-align:text-bottom; }
.sie-consent a { color:#1e66f5; text-decoration:underline; }
.forgot-password-link { margin:10px 0 0; }
.forgot-password-link a { color:#1e66f5; text-decoration:underline; }
#sie-auth-reset-form .input, #sie-auth-reset-form input[type="text"] { width:100%; padding:12px 14px; border:1px solid #d4dceb; border-radius:12px; background:#fff; margin-bottom:20px; }
#sie-auth-reset-form .input:focus, #sie-auth-reset-form input[type="text"]:focus { outline:none; border-color:#1e66f5; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(30,102,245,.14); }
.status-message { text-align:center; color:#1e66f5; font-weight:700; padding:12px; background:#eef5ff; border-left:4px solid #1e66f5; border-radius:8px; margin:10px 0; }
.password-reset-error { text-align:center; background:#ffeaea; color:#8b1d1d; border-left:4px solid #dc3545; border-radius:8px; padding:12px; margin-top:10px; }
.password-reset-success { text-align:center; background:#eaf9ef; color:#14532d; border-left:4px solid #22c55e; border-radius:8px; padding:12px; margin-top:10px; }
body.sie-auth-open .grecaptcha-badge { visibility:visible !important; opacity:1 !important; z-index:2147483647 !important; }
.sie-auth-illustration { display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:flex-end; margin:18px 0 6px; position:relative; padding-bottom:4px; }
.sie-auth-illustration::before { content:""; position:absolute; bottom:0; left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%); width:min(78%,420px); height:26px; border-radius:999px; background:radial-gradient(closest-side,rgba(30,102,245,.18),rgba(30,102,245,0)); filter:blur(6px); pointer-events:none; }
.sie-auth-illustration .hero-image { width:min(92%,420px); height:auto; display:block; filter:drop-shadow(0 14px 26px rgba(30,102,245,.16)); }
@media (max-width:420px){ .sie-auth-illustration .hero-image { width:92%; } }
/* ==================== DESTINATIONS PANEL ==================== */

.sie-dest-panel { position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:2147483000; display:flex; align-items:stretch; justify-content:flex-end; opacity:0; visibility:hidden; pointer-events:none; transition:opacity .25s ease,visibility .25s; }
.sie-dest-panel.open { opacity:1; visibility:visible; pointer-events:auto; }

.sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet { transform:translateX(0); opacity:1; }
@media (max-width:767px){

}
.sie-dest-panel__header { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; margin-bottom:6px; flex-shrink:0; }
.sie-dest-panel__titlewrap { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; }
.sie-dest-panel__globe { font-size:22px; color:#1e66f5; line-height:1; }
.sie-dest-panel__title { font-size:1.5rem; font-weight:800; color:#0b3770; margin:0; line-height:1.2; }
.sie-dest-panel__close { background:transparent; border:0; font-size:22px; color:#0b3770; cursor:pointer; padding:6px 8px; border-radius:8px; line-height:1; opacity:.75; transition:opacity .15s,background .15s; flex-shrink:0; }
.sie-dest-panel__close:hover { opacity:1; background:#f0f4ff; }
.sie-dest-panel__sub { color:#466087; font-size:.94rem; margin:0 0 20px; flex-shrink:0; }
.sie-dest-panel__grid { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr); gap:14px; flex:1; align-content:start; }
@media (max-width:620px){ .sie-dest-panel__grid { grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr); gap:10px; } }
@media (min-width:621px) and (max-width:860px){ .sie-dest-panel__grid { grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr); } }
.sie-dest-panel__card { position:relative; display:block; aspect-ratio:3/2; border-radius:12px; overflow:hidden; text-decoration:none; background:#1d3557; }

 opacity: 0;

 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {

 .sie-dest-panel__titlewrap {

<span><span>sandoel</span></span>

<div class="ecl"><h2><strong>What is the Conference?</strong></h2>

<p>The <strong>Conference on the Future of Europe </strong>is the first transnational discussion with Europeans on how to address Europe’s challenges together. This is an opportunity to think about what citizens and&nbsp; civil society want for the European Union.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

  <div class="eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><h2><strong>How does the Conference work?</strong></h2>

<p>Europeans can share ideas via the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Multilingual Digital Platform</a>, and both national and&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/assemblies/citizens-panels" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">European Citizens' Panels</a>. These contributions feed into the&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/plenary" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference Plenaries</a>.</p>

<p>The Conference&nbsp;offers a new public forum for an open, inclusive, and transparent debate with citizens around a number of key priorities and challenges.</p>

<h2><strong>How can you participate?</strong></h2>

<ul>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]--><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/processes?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">share your own ideas or support others’ ideas</a> on the multilingual digital Conference platform</li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->organise your own events and promote it by adding them to the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference platform</a></li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->take a look at the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/meetings" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">events organised by people across the EU</a></li>
</ul>

<h2><strong>What will the outcome be?</strong></h2>

<p>All of the ideas gathered and reports on events are published on the platform openly and transparently. These reports will then directly influence the discussions in the European Citizens’ Panels as well as in the Plenaries, where citizens will enter into a dialogue with national and European decision makers.</p>

<p>By spring 2022, the Conference will provide guidance on the future of Europe to the European institutions</p>

<p><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/getinvolved" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Get involved and make your voice heard when it comes to education, culture, youth, sport, and more</a>.</p>

<p>Follow on Twitter at&nbsp;</p>

<item>
  <title>European Student Card Initiative at EAIE 2026 in Glasgow - main highlights</title>
  <link>https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/european-student-card-initiative/news/european-student-card-initiative-at-eaie-2026-in-glasgow-main-highlights</link>
  <description>
<h1 class="title-h1 eac-page-title">European Student Card Initiative at EAIE 2026 in Glasgow - main highlights</h1>
<span><span>holbobe</span></span>
<span><time datetime="2026-09-30T09:11:45+02:00" title="Wednesday, September 30, 2026 - 09:11">Wed, 09/30/2026 - 09:11</time>
</span>
<div class="ecl"><p>EAIE 2026 took place from 8 to 11 September, with this year’s theme being “The Rhythm of Revolution”. ESCI featured in five activities: two sessions in the main conference programme and three mini-sessions at the European Commission stand.</p><h2>Shaping the next phase of the ESCI</h2><p>The session “What’s next for the European Student Card Initiative?” brought together Victor Aguilar Mendez from the European Commission, Harpa Sif Arnarsdóttir from RANNIS and Sergi Martínez Rigol from the University of Barcelona to discuss the roadmap beyond 2027.</p><p>The discussion highlighted three main points:</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="ec04a08fab5a0a15faf6d0537ff166c1e"><strong>Build on strong foundations</strong>. Participants welcomed the ambition to further simplify student mobility and emphasised the importance of building on the progress already achieved. They also noted that digital transformation involves more than technical connections, requiring aligned processes, staff capacity and resources.</li><li data-list-item-id="ec8f6683d0b4c64c36760e88ede263ada"><strong>Give institutions clarity and time to prepare</strong>. Participants highlighted the value of clear information on the <a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/european-student-card-initiative/about/esci-2028-2034/continuity-and-preparation?">future scope of ESCI+</a>, practical implications and transition arrangements. The European Commission indicated that 2028 and 2029 are envisaged as transition years.</li><li data-list-item-id="e8a2629faf233a9053a3e7c84c25e2248"><strong>Broaden engagement beyond international relations and IT teams</strong>. Participants highlighted the value of involving university leadership, national authorities, governance bodies and research and education networks.</li></ul><h2>Practical exchange at the European Commission stand</h2><p>Three mini-sessions created space for practical discussion and peer exchange at the European Commission stand:</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="ea46800eaa0963f636bf8742a636fe844"><strong>Digital Officers and ESCI Champions</strong>: “Meet and Greet” explored different opportunities for close collaboration and participants discussed faster communication channels, technical sub-groups and ways to strengthen the community of practitioners.</li><li data-list-item-id="e722608eb7be29071793748afb04db370"><strong>ESCI+ timeline: what to expect and when</strong>, focused on preparations in 2026 and plans for 2027. Participants asked for timely communication, hands-on training, transition arrangements and support to integrate future developments with existing systems.</li><li data-list-item-id="e4abeb75d22c4e87d628dd3a9174bdc0a"><strong>How to issue your first European Student Card</strong> introduced the practical tools available to card issuers, including the ESC Router and the ESC Service Manager for listing services available to ESC holders.</li></ul><h2>Poster session: “The European Student Card: Bridging borders for students”</h2><p>The poster attracted strong interest, with ESCI representatives Elodie Ham (EACEA) and Deborah Arnold (NTT DATA) engaging with participants on the ESCI components and discussing the implications of the ESCI+ timeline with those already involved in the initiative as well as with potential newcomers.</p><h2>Session by ESCI Champions: “Erasmus Without Paper: Getting on board with the digitisation of Erasmus+"&nbsp;</h2></div>
<div class="ecl-u-type-bold ecl-u-mb-m">Intro Text</div><div class="eac-hero"><p>We joined more than 7,300 international education professionals from over 100 countries in Glasgow to discuss what comes next for the European Student Card Initiative and share practical guidance with institutions.</p></div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question">Your institution has a strategy and an overarching structure supporting internationalisation</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The internationalisation strategy is available and prominently displayed on your website</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Internationalisation is an important driver for institutional change, and has a great influence on the major activities of a higher education institution (HEI) i.e. education and research. The importance of internationalisation is recognised, and most institutions have a strategy for internationalisation. However, for a strategy to be efficient, and for it to drive the HEI's activities regarding internationalisation, there is a need for its acceptance from across the whole institution. In addition the strategy could also be accessible to external collaborative partners. It is highly important to have the institution's internationalisation and modernisation strategy published and easily accessible to all.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution has a clear plan to implement the strategy</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The strategy and policy should include explicit allocation of responsibilities for its efficient implementation to individuals at all levels of the institution, from senior management to the heads of departments, schools and faculties, to academic and administrative staff. This will ensure acceptance and accountability for the strategy. The internationalisation strategy and policy should outline a specific implementation plan that sets out explicitly the financial and human resources available.&nbsp; For example, it is recommended to set up an International Relations Office (IRO) to implement mobility and other international projects.</p><p>As with any other activity, the institutional implementation of the internationalisation strategy is dependent on the people behind the activities. It is highly important for an institution to have staff with the right set of skills and knowledge driving the internationalisation agenda and liaising with international students and staff members. Therefore understanding the development needs of the staff and supporting their professional development should be a high priority for the institution. Such development should focus on both staff engaged in international activities as well as the supporting staff, ensuring the most efficient implementation of international activities and cooperative projects across the institution. For example, trainings/webinars/projects could be organised on intercultural competences and communication, project management, enhancement of internationalisation at home/intercultural, or other activities suggested by the staff and supported by the hierarchy.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It promotes incoming and outgoing student and staff mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobility is important to the development of the institution as a whole as well as for the individual participants. Therefore the HEI should make mobility and international cooperation a central element in its institutional policies, and explicitly and consistently promote and support student and staff mobility. Non-discrimination policies and further emphasis on the promotion of mobility for under-represented groups should also form an integral part of the institutional support structures.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It promotes engagement in European and international cooperation projects</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution's internationalisation strategy and policy should explicitly and consistently promote the development of cooperation with partners in other EU and non-EU countries. The activities and co-operation projects agreed by the HEI should be based on identified needs. In addition they should identify geographical and subject priorities of the internationalisation strategy.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The implementation of the strategic plan is monitored</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>International activity, including co-operation projects and mobility should be carefully monitored. Clear and unambiguous monitoring of such activity are key to ensuring success. Explicit indicators should be developed to show specific success scenarios. The indicators should be SMART.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Incentives are provided to staff involved in international activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in such international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI. It should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation. As part of the institutional modernisation and internationalisation strategy, concrete support measures should be defined at both institutional and departmental levels to encourage and recognise staff participating in such projects, as well as allow adequate time to carry out this work.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-effective-management-and-ownership-of-erasmus-for-internationalisation" target="_blank">The effective management and ownership of Erasmus +’ for ‘internationalisation’</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/internationalisation-at-the-university-of-helsinki" target="_blank">Internationalisation at the University of Helsinki </a></div>
                                             </div>

                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>In signing the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education, the institution agrees to respect <strong>in full</strong> the principles of non-discrimination as set out in the Programme. The institution must clearly demonstrate through its policies, rules and regulations that equal access and opportunities to mobile participants from all backgrounds. Which means that all individuals or groups will be treated equally, irrespective of their characteristics. In accordance with Article 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, there should be no discrimination "based on sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation". For more information, see: <a href="http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf">http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf</a></p>                      </div>

                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Ensuring that the mobile participant, sending and receiving HEI/organisation/enterprise (i.e. all three parties) sign the Learning Agreement before the start of the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The purpose of the Learning Agreement is to provide a transparent and efficient preparation of the study period abroad and to ensure that the student will receive recognition in his/her degree for the educational components or traineeship successfully completed abroad. The Learning Agreement:</p><ul><li>Sets out the learning outcomes for the mobility, including both the educational components or traineeship activities to be carried out by the student at the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise, which will be recognised by the sending institution upon successful completion of the study programme abroad and counted towards his/her degree.</li><li>Ensures full recognition for satisfactorily completed activities of study mobility and traineeships in terms of credits awarded, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams, and documents these credits in the student records, so that they can be identified in a transparent way.</li></ul><p>The Learning Agreement is binding for all parties and constitutes the cornerstone of successful student mobility (for studies, traineeships, and combinations thereof), including quality assurances and the process for transparent transfer of credits. Therefore, it is essential to conduct mobility based on an agreed and signed Learning Agreement. The Learning Agreement should be agreed and signed by all parties (the student, the sending institution and the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise) before the start of the mobility. It is not compulsory to circulate papers with original signatures; scanned copies of signatures or digital signatures may be accepted, depending on the national legislation.</p><p>The EU official templates for Learning Agreements for studies and traineeships are available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm&nbsp;&nbsp;</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Including allocation of responsibility to an academic who has the authority to approve, amend and recognise the Learning Agreements on behalf of the responsible academic body</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The formal procedures for recognising student mobility should clearly and unambiguously set out the responsibilities of an appointed academic, who has the authority, on behalf of the appropriate academic body, to:</p><ul><li>Approve the Learning Agreements,</li><li>Exceptionally amend the Learning Agreements, and</li><li>Recognise the successfully completed activities, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams.</li></ul>                      </div>

                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Ensuring that the mobile participant, sending and receiving HEI/organisation/enterprise (i.e. all three parties) sign the Learning Agreement before the start of the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The purpose of the Learning Agreement is to provide a transparent and efficient preparation of the study period abroad and to ensure that the student will receive recognition in his/her degree for the educational components or traineeship successfully completed abroad. The Learning Agreement:</p><ul><li>Sets out the learning outcomes for the mobility, including both the educational components or traineeship activities to be carried out by the student at the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise, which will be recognised by the sending institution upon successful completion of the study programme abroad and counted towards his/her degree.</li><li>Ensures full recognition for satisfactorily completed activities of study mobility and traineeships in terms of credits awarded, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams, and documents these credits in the student records, so that they can be identified in a transparent way.</li></ul><p>The Learning Agreement is binding for all parties and constitutes the cornerstone of successful student mobility (for studies, traineeships, and combinations thereof), including quality assurances and the process for transparent transfer of credits.                                                 <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Ensuring that the mobile participant, sending and receiving institution/organisation/enterprise (i.e. all three parties) sign the mobility agreement before the start of the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>To ensure effective staff mobility, it has to be based on a signed mobility agreement. The mobility agreement has to acceptable and signed by all parties in advance. There are four key elements set out by the mobility agreement, which are intended to increase the relevance and potential impact of the mobility. These are:</p><ul><li>The overall objectives and academic rationale of the mobility,</li><li>The institutional requirements or strategy, and the mobility's added value in the context of modernisation and internationalisation,</li><li>The activities or teaching programme content to be undertaken by the staff member, and,</li><li>The expected outcomes and impact of the mobility on the professional development of the staff member at both institutions.</li></ul><p>For this to work effectively, there needs to be dialogue and discussion between the three parties prior to the signing of the mobility agreement having agreed the common goals which are acceptable.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">

                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q10.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> During the mobility, your institution fosters the integration of the incoming mobile participants</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution appoints responsible person(s) to deal with practical issues (e.g. social, health, and/or psychological problems)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution should ensure there are named, visible persons who are responsible for the practical issues associated with integrating mobile students. This visibility should be ensured through introduction to this function during the Welcome / Orientation period and be detailed on the website so all mobile students can easily access this support, throughout their stay.&nbsp;</p><p>Non-academic mentoring and support arrangements should already be outlined in the Course Catalogue of the receiving HEI, in the section on general information for students, with relevant contact persons in the respective areas. Academic advisors should have close contact with the practical services which are available to incoming participants as they are often the first line of contact to the incoming student. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>

                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                     </div>
    </div>
</div>

{"data":[{"slug":"head-of-marketing-leverkusen-164842","company_name":"THEFABERS","title":"Head of Marketing (m/w/d)","description":"

THEFABERS die Spezialeinheit, wenn es darum geht, Landingpages zu bauen, die nicht nur Klicks sammeln – sondern Kassen füllen. Unsere Kunden? Marken mit Hunger. Marken, die Tempo lieben, Budgets bewegen und Ergebnisse sehen wollen.

Hier läuft kein endloses Abstimmungskarussell. Hier zählt nur eins: Speed. Impact. Resultate.

Wir verbinden knallhartes Marketing-Know-how mit Design, das verführt, und Copywriting, das verkauft – und wir setzen um, bevor andere noch diskutieren.

Bei uns führst du nicht kleine Kampagnen, du steuerst Projekte, die Umsatzkurven sprengen. Du arbeitest Schulter an Schulter mit A-Playern, die dich fordern, fördern – und mit dir zusammen gewinnen wollen.

Hier geht es nicht darum, mitzuschwimmen – sondern Wellen zu machen.

Aufgaben

Du bist die Schaltzentrale zum Kunden – die Person, die den Überblick behält, klare Ansagen macht und trotzdem menschlich nah dran ist.

  • Du führst Projekte von der ersten Funken-Idee bis zum Launch, hältst Timelines wie ein Dirigent den Takt und sorgst dafür, dass jeder im Team weiß, was als Nächstes kommt.
  • Du entwirfst die DNA unserer Landingpages – du kennst die Zielgruppe wie deine Westentasche, triffst ins Mark ihrer Bedürfnisse und baust Strukturen, die Leads magnetisch anziehen.
  • Du schreibst Texte, die treffen wie ein Volltreffer im Finale – psychologisch messerscharf, glasklar in der Botschaft und gebaut, um zu konvertieren.

Qualifikation

Was du mitbringen solltest:

  • Projektmanagement-Erfahrung – idealerweise im Agentur- oder Online-Marketing-Umfeld.
  • Copywriting-Fähigkeiten – du kannst präzise, verkaufsstark und zielgruppenorientiert schreiben.
  • Marketingverständnis – du verstehst, wie Conversion entsteht und wie man Menschen überzeugt.
  • Strukturiertes Arbeiten – du hältst Timings, steuerst Prozesse und gehst proaktiv voran.
  • Leadership – du kannst zuhören, beraten und Verantwortung übernehmen.

Benefits

Was wir dir bieten:

🌍 Remote Work – arbeite von wo du willst.

🧠 Weiterbildung & Mentoring – wachse persönlich & fachlich.

💡 Verantwortung & Gestaltungsspielraum – deine Ideen zählen.

💪 Ein echtes Team aus A-Playern – kein Bullshit, kein Ego, nur starke Leute.

🎉 Workations & Team-Events – wir arbeiten hart und feiern klug.

Was dich erwartet:

💬 Direkte Kommunikation mit Kunden, bei der du souverän durch Projekte führst und Erwartungen übertriffst.

🧠 Strategische Planung von Landingpages, die nicht nur hübsch aussehen, sondern echte Conversion bringen.

✍️ Copywriting mit Wirkung – du formulierst Headlines, Struktur & USPs so, dass sie verkaufen.

📅 Projektmanagement vom Kick-off bis Go-Live – mit klarem Blick für Zeitpläne, Qualität & Deadlines.

🎯 Ergebnisorientiertes Arbeiten in einem A-Player-Team, das für messbare Wirkung und starke Marken lebt.

Über Simba Computer Systeme GmbH

Gestalte heute mit uns, was morgen zählt – mit Teamgeist, einem guten Gespür für Menschen und dem Anspruch, gemeinsam unsere Personalarbeit weiterzuentwickeln. Bei Simba findest du ein Umfeld, das auf klare Prozesse, echtes Miteinander und kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung setzt – fachlich und menschlich.

Als Personalreferent (m/w/d) bist du Teil unseres HR-Teams und begleitest gemeinsam mit uns unsere Mitarbeiter & Mitarbeiterinnen durch den Arbeitsalltag. Dabei übernimmst du eigene Aufgabenbereiche, sorgst für eine zuverlässige Personaladministration und bringst deine Erfahrung in der Entgeltabrechnung ein. Gleichzeitig befinden wir uns mitten in der Weiterentwicklung unserer HR-Prozesse und der Implementierung von REXX – hier kannst du aktiv mitgestalten und deine Ideen einbringen.

Auf dich wartet eine noch frische HR-Abteilung mit vielseitigen Themen, kurzen Entscheidungswegen und viel Raum, eigene Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

Klingt das nach dir? Dann bewirb dich beim #TeamSimba und lass uns zusammen mehr erreichen!

WAS SIND DEINE AUFGABEN?

  • Personaladministration: du übernimmst eigenständig administrative HR-Aufgaben vom Eintritt bis zum Austritt und sorgst für eine zuverlässige Pflege unserer Personalstammdaten und -unterlagen

  • Personalbetreuung: gemeinsam im Team bist du Ansprechpartner für unsere Mitarbeiter & Mitarbeiterinnen bei personalrelevanten Fragestellungen

  • HR-Prozesse: du wirkst bei der Gestaltung neuer und der Weiterentwicklung bestehender Personalprozesse mit und bringst dabei deine Erfahrungen und Ideen ein

  • Payroll: du betreust unsere monatliche Lohn- und Gehaltsabrechnung und kümmerst dich zuverlässig um alle dazugehörigen abrechnungsrelevanten Themen

  • REXX: du unterstützt aktiv bei der Implementierung unseres neuen HR-Systems und wirkst dabei mit, unsere Prozesse sinnvoll und praxisnah im System abzubilden

  • Zusammenarbeit: du arbeitest eng mit unseren Abteilungen und Führungskräften zusammen und sorgst gemeinsam im Team für verlässliche und praktikable Lösungen

WAS BRINGST DU MIT?

  • Erfahrung: mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Personalbereich sowie praktische Erfahrung in der Personaladministration und Personalbetreuung

  • Payroll: fundierte Kenntnisse in der Lohn- und Gehaltsabrechnung sowie im Lohnsteuer- und Sozialversicherungsrecht

  • Gerne gesehen: Erfahrung mit REXX oder einem vergleichbaren HR-System, belastbare Kenntnisse in der Abrechnung bspw. mit SBS, sowie Freude daran, digitale HR-Prozesse mitzugestalten

  • Persönlichkeit: kommunikativ, verbindlich und zuverlässig sowie eine strukturierte, sorgfältige und eigenständige Arbeitsweise

  • Ausbildung: abgeschlossenes Studium oder Berufsausbildung mit Schwerpunkt Personal, BWL oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation

  • Sprachkenntnisse: verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse Deine Benefits

WAS BIETEN WIR DIR?

  • Onboarding: fundierte und professionelle Einarbeitung, sowie enge Begleitung durch einen Mentor

  • Ausstattung: modern und ergonomisch ausgestattete Arbeitsplätze, hochwertige IT-Ausstattung

  • Work-Life-Balance: flexible Arbeitszeiten mit Zeiterfassung und Gleitzeitkonto, Option auf mobiles Arbeiten, 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Gehaltspaket: attraktives und leistungsgerechtes Gehalt, inkl. großzügigem Weihnachtsgeld

  • Mitarbeiterangebote: Kostenlose Getränke und leckeren Kaffee, Corporate Benefit Programm, Team-Events, Zahnzusatzversicherung, sowie individuelle Angebote in unseren Niederlassungen (Eis-Flatrate im Sommer, Kanu-Tour oder Whiskey Tasting)

  • Weiterentwicklung: stetige Weiterentwicklung und gezielte Förderung der persönlichen – und fachlichen Skills

  • Unternehmenskultur: offene Feedbackkultur, flache Hierarchien, kollegiale Du-Kultur, ein wertschätzender Umgang und die Möglichkeit dich aktiv mit deinen Ideen bei uns einzubringen

NOCH FRAGEN?

In den ersten Wochen wirst du intensiv in unsere internen Abläufe und die Besonderheiten Bei Rückfragen zur Position oder unserem Bewerbungsprozess stehen wir dir gerne zur Verfügung.

Nina König
